prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  tan: 0.60
  gal: 0.40
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_D:
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2005 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core values and approach
- Principles: Freedom, Fairness, Trust, with a “green thread” through all policies and strong internationalism.
- Funding: Switch ~£5bn/yr from low-priority spend (abolish DTI, scrap ID cards, redirect Child Trust Fund). One tax rise: 50% rate on income over £100,000 to fund scrapping tuition fees, free personal care, and lower local taxes via replacing Council Tax with a fairer Local Income Tax (typical household saves ~£450). Raise stamp duty threshold to £150,000.

Health
- Free personal care for elderly and disabled, implement Royal Commission.
- Faster diagnosis using all capacity; more evening/weekend scans; publish test waits; train staff to use scanners.
- Free eye/dental checks; extend prescription charge exemptions; rebuild NHS dentistry.
- Recruit 8,000 doctors, 12,000 nurses, 18,000 therapists; cut central targets, empower local decision-making.
- Personal care plans, stronger mental health rights; end age discrimination.
- Prevention: school nutrition standards, restrict junk-food ads, healthy vending rules; ban smoking in enclosed public places.

Education and skills
- Abolish tuition and top-up fees; restore maintenance grants.
- Cut class sizes (infants avg 20; juniors 25) by using Child Trust Fund money; extend 8am–6pm provision; expand Children’s Centres.
- Qualified teachers in core subjects; reduce high-stakes testing; stronger discipline support.
- Better SEN provision; 14–19 diploma blending academic/vocational; equal funding for equivalent courses; invest in college facilities; protect school transport rights.

Crime, liberty, immigration
- 10,000 extra police funded by scrapping ID cards; complete 20,000 CSOs; cut police bureaucracy.
- Community payback; targeted action on binge drinking; rehabilitation and skills in prisons tied to release.
- Create UK Border Force; prosecute terror in mainstream courts; admit intercept evidence; repeal flawed control-order law.
- Fair, faster asylum via a dedicated agency; allow asylum seekers to work. Single Equality Act; hate-crime units.

Economy and business
- Fiscal stability with independent NAO scrutiny; ONS independence; rein in irresponsible lending.
- Fairer, simpler taxes; consult on business tax reform; managed economic migration.
- Slash red tape (impact tests, sunset clauses, single inspectorate); small business rate relief (up to £1,500); abolish DTI and redirect funds; legal duty to trade fairly; boost tourism.
- Green economy: convert Climate Change Levy to Carbon Tax; at least 20% electricity from renewables by 2020; no new nuclear; stronger incentives for clean cars/homes.

Pensions and benefits
- Citizen’s Pension from 75: £109.45 (single), £167.05 (couple), earnings-linked; reduce means-testing. Local Income Tax benefits 8/10 pensioners.
- Maternity Income Guarantee: £170/week for 6 months for first child.
- Reform New Deal; scrap CSA (move to Inland Revenue with tribunal appeals); Winter Fuel Payment for severely disabled; bolster pensions compensation; cut fraud/error; insulation vouchers to cut bills.

Communities, housing, culture
- Replace Council Tax with Local Income Tax.
- 100,000 affordable homes on public land; VAT reform to favour brownfield/renovation; planning permission for second homes in pressured areas.
- Restore Lottery independence; protect post offices and universal mail; devolve powers; streamline inspections.
- Waste: 60% household recycling in 7 years; zero-waste goal; climate-conscious planning/building regs.

International, Europe, defence, development
- Opposed Iraq war; support transition and aim to withdraw by UN mandate end; rebuild multilateralism, UN reform, Middle East peace.
- Support EU Constitution via referendum; prepare to join euro when conditions met.
- Armed forces: end overstretch; improve procurement; cut Eurofighter Tranche 3; share burdens via NATO/EU; retain minimum deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament; tighter arms export controls.
- Aid to 0.5% GNI by 2007/08 and 0.7% by 2011; fairer trade, end dumping; green, sustainable development; lead on climate with “contraction and convergence.”

Rural and environment
- Fair farm prices (duty to trade fairly; Food Trade Inspector); CAP/CFP reform; Marine Act; Animal Welfare Act and Commission; precaution on GM, support organics.

Transport
- Reform rail franchising; restore key upgrades; improve station safety.
- Reward low-emission cars (VED reform); expand congestion charging; long-term national road pricing to replace fuel duty/VED.
- Free off-peak buses for pensioners/disabled; free railcards for eligible groups; limit new road-building; boost public transport, rail freight, waterways; per-aircraft aviation charges; oppose new/expanded SE airports; protect lifeline routes.

Better government
- Curb PM powers (War Powers Act), Civil Service Act, stronger Select Committees; predominantly elected second chamber; STV for Commons and local/devolved; votes at 16; devolve quango powers; fair funding across UK.
- Make BBC independent via external regulator; Environmental Responsibility Act; green public procurement; create an Environment-Transport-Energy department.

TEXT_F:
Conservative Party Manifesto 2005 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core message: Britain has great potential but is heading in the wrong direction under Labour. The Conservatives promise action over talk, rewarding hard work, restoring accountability, devolving power, and focusing on practical priorities: cleaner hospitals, school discipline, more police, controlled immigration and lower taxes.

Economy and tax:
- Cut waste and borrowing to fund tax cuts: save £12bn/year by 2007–08 (civil service freeze, 235,000 fewer bureaucratic posts, scrap/merge 168 bodies); use £8bn to reduce borrowing and £4bn for tax cuts.
- Lower, simpler taxes to promote work and enterprise; keep minimum wage and planned rises.
- Halve council tax bills (up to £500) for households where all residents are over 65, funded centrally.
- Pensions: restore earnings link for the basic state pension; keep Winter Fuel Payment, over-75 TV licences, and 2005 council tax payment. Create Lifetime Savings Accounts; strengthen workplace pensions (opt-out schemes); use unclaimed financial assets to protect failed scheme members.
- Stability: keep Bank of England independence; no to the Euro. Deregulation via regulatory budgets, sunset reviews, end EU “gold-plating”; restore UK opt-out from EU Social Chapter.

Education and families:
- Flexible childcare: more flexible maternity pay; up to £50/week per under-5 via Working Tax Credit for all qualifying working families, usable for formal or informal care; support workplace nurseries and after-school clubs.
- Restore discipline: give heads/governors full control over admissions/expulsions; Turnaround Schools for disruptive pupils; protect teachers from malicious allegations; slash paperwork; funding to follow the pupil.
- Raise standards: scrap grade-inflation targets; publish marks alongside grades; allow international qualifications; slim and depoliticise the National Curriculum; 300,000 vocational grants for 14–16s; more sport (two hours after-school) and ban junk food in schools.
- Higher/further education: scrap university tuition fees; abolish the admissions regulator; build endowments; simplify FE funding and empower “super colleges.”

NHS and social care:
- Increase NHS funding by £34bn over the Parliament; shift power to professionals; abolish Strategic Health Authorities, cut PCTs and quangos; end central targets; funding to follow patients; more single rooms and infection control; restore matrons with power to close wards; protect community hospitals.
- End waiting lists as we know them; offer NHS contribution (half NHS cost) for self-pay operations to cut queues.
- Reform dentistry (low monthly payment option); more support for carers; partnership scheme so no one must sell their home for long-term care.
- Health checks for long-stay non-EU migrants; STI public health campaign.

Crime and security:
- 5,000 extra police officers each year; slash paperwork; elected police commissioners; genuine neighbourhood policing.
- 20,000 extra prison places; end early release; honesty in sentencing.
- Drugs: 25,000 residential rehab places; hard-drug users: treatment or court; reclassify cannabis to Class B.
- Appoint a Homeland Security Minister; robust counter-terror measures.

Immigration and borders:
- Controlled immigration with popular consent: 24/7 port surveillance, restored embarkation controls, create a British Border Control Police.
- Australian-style points system prioritising needed skills.
- Asylum: repatriate powers from the EU; replace the 1951 Geneva framework with modern agreements; process claims outside the UK; fixed annual refugee quota via UNHCR; overall annual immigration limit set by Parliament.

Constitution, communities, and environment:
- Accountability: Timetable for Action; ministers who fail will go. Abolish regional assemblies; strengthen Parliament and select committees; cut MPs by 20%; English votes for English laws.
- Devolution: back the Union; Welsh referendum on Assembly powers; stricter standards for NI executive participation.
- Localism: devolve planning/housing/transport/fire to councils; tougher action on illegal traveller camps; devolve arts and Lottery decisions.
- Housing: extend Right to Buy to housing association tenants; expand shared ownership.
- Transport: end “war on motorists”; modernise roads; review all speed cameras; longer rail franchises.
- Environment: protect Green Belt, prioritise brownfield; phase out HFCs; lower VED for low-emission cars; boost home energy efficiency; expand renewables and energy security; more recycling.
- Rural/agriculture: honest food labelling; require Little Red Tractor in public procurement; push CAP reform; strengthen animal welfare; free vote to overturn hunting ban.

Foreign policy and defence:
- Spend £2.7bn more on the military front line by 2007–08; preserve regiments and warships; NATO at the core; support service families.
- Iraq: stay to rebuild and support democracy; pursue Middle East peace (secure Israel and viable Palestinian state).
- Europe: oppose EU Constitution (referendum within six months); no Euro; restore Social Chapter opt-out; repatriate fisheries control; back enlargement including Turkey.
- Aid: meet 0.7% of GNI by 2013; increase UK control of aid; champion open markets, rule of law and property rights.

First-month actions: begin recruiting 5,000 extra police per year; restore matrons; first Budget to cut waste and lower taxes; empower heads to expel; start 24/7 port surveillance; set date for EU Constitution referendum (campaign for No).
